A stack of only-just-happened facts is the <vocabulary form="ニュース">news</vocabulary>, and you ask for it as <reading>ニュース</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 記（き）＋事（じ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A recorded (記) matter (事): an article.
items.meaning_mnemonic: An <vocabulary form="記事">article</vocabulary> is a <kanji form="記">written account</kanji> of exactly one <kanji form="事">matter</kanji>, pinned down so hard it cannot wriggle off the page before you finish reading.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 翻（ほん）＋訳（やく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Turning over (翻) meaning (訳): translation.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="翻訳">translation</vocabulary> is made by taking the foreign page, giving it one full <kanji form="翻">flip</kanji>, and <kanji form="訳">translating</kanji> the side now facing you into words you can read.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 市（し）＋役（やく）＋所（しょ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The city's (市) work office (役所): city hall.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The one <kanji form="所">place</kanji> in the <kanji form="市">city</kanji> where every civic <kanji form="役">duty</kanji> gets handled — a birth registered, a tax paid, a form filed — is the <vocabulary form="市役所">city hall</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋学（がく）＋院（いん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: University's (大学) inner court (院): grad school.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <vocabulary form="大学院">graduate school</vocabulary> is the <kanji form="院">institution</kanji> you climb to only after a full degree, where the <kanji form="学">studying</kanji> is a <kanji form="大">big</kanji>ger version of everything you did downstairs.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 必（かなら）＋ず.
items.mnemonic_text: A resolved heart pierced through: certainly.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Dodging a slash aimed at your heart is not a choice your body makes. It happens every time because the move is <kanji form="必">necessary</kanji>, and something that locked-in happens <vocabulary form="必ず">definitely / without fail</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kana the courier has never missed one delivery, in storms or on holidays. The way <reading>Kana rushes</reading> it out every single time is <reading>かならず</reading>, <vocabulary form="必ず">definitely / without fail</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Right or wrong, just do it: zehi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hesitate on the step, and the innkeeper throws the door wide with a bright <reading>Zee, hi</reading> and waves you straight in. That whole-hearted come-right-in is <reading>ぜひ</reading>, <vocabulary form="ぜひ">by all means</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Setting up a hypothetical: moshi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Rain has turned the riverbank path to <reading>mushy</reading> mud. The guide says that <reading>もし</reading> your boots sink in you should turn back, the word that sets up a plain <vocabulary form="もし">if (hypothetical)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 例（たと）＋えば.
items.mnemonic_text: Comparing (例) if (えば): for instance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To pin down what 'a bird' means you hold up one sparrow and one crow and let those two stand in for the whole idea. Reaching for a specific case to carry the general one is <vocabulary form="例えば">for example</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The artist at the <reading>tattoo bar</reading> never describes a style in words. She flips to one drawing, says <reading>たとえば</reading> this dragon, and lets that single sample do the defining, which is <vocabulary form="例えば">for example</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Packed down to the point: tsumari.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the end of class the teacher wipes the board and writes one short line under everything that was there. Boiling the whole hour down to that single <reading>summary</reading> is <reading>つまり</reading>, <vocabulary form="つまり">in other words</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Adding yet another layer: sara ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On your first morning the manager lists the small perks, then adds one more item on top, the <reading>salary</reading>. Stacking that extra point onto what was already said is <reading>さらに</reading>, <vocabulary form="さらに">furthermore</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — その＋上（うえ）.
items.mnemonic_text: On top (上) of that (その): moreover.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Put the new point <kanji form="上">above</kanji> the one you just made, one slab laid on top of another. That stacking of a second thing over the first is <vocabulary form="その上">moreover</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: On its own 上 is read 「うえ」, the sound you already know, so <vocabulary form="その上">moreover</vocabulary> simply ends that way and is <reading>そのうえ</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Shifting the place of topic: tokorode.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Mid-conversation on the highway, the driver <reading>took a road</reading> off to the right with no warning and opened a whole new subject. Swerving the talk onto another route is <reading>ところで</reading>, <vocabulary form="ところで">by the way</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A firm certainty: kitto.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The locksmith lifts one blank off the ring, holds it to the light, and says it is <reading>key to</reading> this lock with no doubt at all. That flat certainty before he has even tried it is <reading>きっと</reading>, <vocabulary form="きっと">surely / certainly</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Disbelief at the impossible: masaka.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You kick the ball in the backyard, look up, and <reading>my soccer</reading> ball is somehow up on the roof across the street, the jolt of cannot-be that we blurt as <reading>まさか</reading>, <vocabulary form="まさか">no way! / surely not</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: On'yomi — 別（べつ）＋に.
items.mnemonic_text: Nothing special going on: betsu ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Something you can keep <kanji form="別">separate</kanji> from what matters is not worth bringing up, so when nothing is really on your mind you answer <vocabulary form="別に">not particularly</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 一（いっ）＋層（そう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 一 いち → いっ.
items.mnemonic_text: One (一) more layer (層): even more.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stack <kanji form="一">one</kanji> more <kanji form="層">layer</kanji> onto a pile that is already high, and the whole thing presses down <vocabulary form="一層">even more</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 次（し）＋第（だい）＋に, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Step by step in sequence: shidai ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Work through the list in <kanji form="次">order</kanji>, moving from one <kanji form="第">number</kanji> to the next, and the whole thing shifts <vocabulary form="次第に">gradually</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 何（なん）＋となく.
items.mnemonic_text: Without quite knowing why: nantonaku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When something tugs at you but you cannot say <kanji form="何">what</kanji> it is, that faint pull is <vocabulary form="何となく">somehow / vaguely</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Since 何 already gave you 「なん」, this word just rides that sound: <vocabulary form="何となく">somehow / vaguely</vocabulary> is <reading>なんとなく</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Deliberately doing it: wazato.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At Grandma Kane's shrine one cat <reading>waltzed to</reading> the bell rope, smooth and unhurried, and hauled it down. A walk that deliberate proves the cat rang the bell <reading>わざと</reading>, that is, <vocabulary form="わざと">on purpose</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Asking what happened: dou shimashita ka.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You walk in on Sei standing over a toy car mashed flat — <reading>dough, she mashed a car</reading> — and the wreck drags the words <reading>どうしましたか</reading> out of you, meaning <vocabulary form="どうしましたか">what's wrong? / what happened?</vocabulary>

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 何（なん）＋ですか.
items.mnemonic_text: A direct query about a thing: nan desu ka.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The word is nothing but the <kanji form="何">what</kanji> kanji asked aloud, which is why it lands on <vocabulary form="何ですか">what is it?</vocabulary>
items.reading_mnemonic: The reading 「なん」 is one you already took from 何, so keep it: <reading>なんですか</reading> is simply <vocabulary form="何ですか">what is it?</vocabulary>

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Both directions apply: dochira mo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Moe the Dutch llama stands with his front feet on one riverbank and his back feet on the other, drinking from <vocabulary form="どちらも">both / either</vocabulary> side at once. Picture that <reading>Dutch llama, Moe</reading> whenever you say <reading>どちらも</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 誰（だれ）＋でも.
items.mnemonic_text: Whoever it may be: dare demo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Point at <kanji form="誰">who</kanji> and stop caring which face the answer picks, and the word opens wide enough to cover <vocabulary form="誰でも">anyone</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You learned 「だれ」 back with 誰, so nothing new to memorise here: <vocabulary form="誰でも">anyone</vocabulary> is <reading>だれでも</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 何（なん）＋でも.
items.mnemonic_text: Whatever it may be: nani demo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Leave <kanji form="何">what</kanji> with no fixed answer in mind and it stretches to take in <vocabulary form="何でも">anything</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The sound 「なん」 is already yours from 何, so just carry it over: <vocabulary form="何でも">anything</vocabulary> is <reading>なんでも</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Wherever it may be: doko demo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Doc lugs his first-aid kit up the mountain trail and runs the same demo wherever a hiker drops — a boulder, the vending machine, the middle of the path. <reading>Doc, oh, demo</reading> here too, so any spot works, and <reading>どこでも</reading> is that: <vocabulary form="どこでも">anywhere</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Whenever it may be: itsu demo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The tasting stand by the onigiri shelf at Koichi's konbini never shuts down; walk in at three in the morning and <reading>it's a demo</reading> running, same as noon. That round-the-clock sampling is <reading>いつでも</reading>, meaning <vocabulary form="いつでも">anytime</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 誰（だれ）＋も.
items.mnemonic_text: Not a single person: dare mo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Call out <kanji form="誰">who</kanji> is there, hear every corner stay silent, and the tally comes to <vocabulary form="誰も">no one (with negative)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: You already have 「だれ」 from 誰, so this one only adds the empty feeling: <vocabulary form="誰も">no one (with negative)</vocabulary> is <reading>だれも</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 何（なに）＋も.
items.mnemonic_text: Not a single thing: nani mo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Ask <kanji form="何">what</kanji> is left in the bag, shake it, and hear <vocabulary form="何も">nothing (with negative)</vocabulary> rattle inside.
items.reading_mnemonic: The reading 「なに」 already came from 何, so keep it as is: <vocabulary form="何も">nothing (with negative)</vocabulary> is <reading>なにも</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Not any place at all: doko mo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Moe checks the first riverbank dock, then the next, then the one past that — <reading>dock, oh, Moe</reading> keeps walking — and the missing boat turns up at <vocabulary form="どこも">nowhere (with negative)</vocabulary>. Say <reading>どこも</reading> and see Moe trudging that empty line of piers.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — どう＋思（おも）＋いますか.
items.mnemonic_text: Asking for an opinion: dou omoimasu ka.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Here the <kanji form="思">think</kanji> kanji stands alone, simply turned outward to ask <vocabulary form="どう思いますか">what do you think?</vocabulary>
items.reading_mnemonic: You picked up 「おも」 from 思う already, so this phrase adds nothing to learn: <reading>どうおもいますか</reading> is just <vocabulary form="どう思いますか">what do you think?</vocabulary>

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — そう＋思（おも）＋います.
items.mnemonic_text: Agreeing with a thought: sou omoimasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Again it is only the <kanji form="思">think</kanji> kanji, this time reporting that you agree, which is <vocabulary form="そう思います">I think so</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: The 「おも」 sound is already yours from 思う, so let it stand: <vocabulary form="そう思います">I think so</vocabulary> is <reading>そうおもいます</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A thoughtful agreement: sou desu ne.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Grandma Kane holds up the torn sleeve and asks if the seam runs here, and you nod slowly — <reading>sew this, eh</reading> — taking a moment before you commit. That slow, agreeing pause is <reading>そうですね</reading>, meaning <vocabulary form="そうですね">that's right / let me think</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 本（ほん）＋当（とう）＋ですか, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Questioning the truth: hontou desu ka.
items.meaning_mnemonic: What holds true to its <kanji form="本">origin</kanji> and lands exactly <kanji form="当">right</kanji> is the plain truth, so to ask whether something really is, you say <vocabulary form="本当ですか">really?</vocabulary>

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Understanding dawning: naruhodo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Watch a barn dance long enough and the tangle of stamping feet suddenly locks into one clear pattern, like a <reading>Nara hoedown</reading> snapping into step. That click of it all making sense is <reading>なるほど</reading>, meaning <vocabulary form="なるほど">I see / indeed</vocabulary>.

items.meaning: thank you for your hard work
items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — お＋疲（つか）＋れ＋様（さま）.
items.mnemonic_text: Honoring someone's tiredness: otsukaresama.

accepted_answers.answer_text: thank you for your hard work

items.meaning_mnemonic: A workmate drops into a chair looking completely <kanji form="疲">weary</kanji>. You greet that tired person in the polite <kanji form="様">manner</kanji> saved for an honoured guest, and that greeting is <vocabulary form="お疲れ様">thank you for your hard work</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋世（せ）＋話（わ）＋になる, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving generational (世) care: osewa ni naru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The people of your <kanji form="世">world</kanji> will not stop <kanji form="話">talking</kanji> about whether you have eaten and slept enough. When a whole family keeps you fed and rested like that, you have come <vocabulary form="お世話になる">to be in someone's care</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 失（しつ）＋礼（れい）＋します, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Politely excusing a discourtesy: shitsurei shimasu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Stepping into someone's office is a tiny <kanji form="失">fault</kanji> against the full <kanji form="礼">bow</kanji> of good manners. You name that small lapse out loud as you enter or leave, and that is <vocabulary form="失礼します">excuse me (entering/leaving)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A joyful blessing: omedetou.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A baker flips a flawless omelette off a lump of fresh <reading>omelette dough</reading>. The whole cafe stands up and shouts <reading>おめでとう</reading>, which is how you say <vocabulary form="おめでとう">congratulations</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Mixed — 頑（がん）on'yomi ＋ 張（ば）kun'yomi ＋ っ ＋ て.
items.mnemonic_text: Encouraging perseverance: ganbatte.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone who is <kanji form="頑">stubborn</kanji> keeps <kanji form="張">stretch</kanji>ing toward a goal long after their arms ache. Telling a friend to be exactly that stubborn is what <vocabulary form="頑張って">good luck / do your best</vocabulary> means.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — お＋大（だい）＋事（じ）＋に, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Wishing importance to their health: odaiji ni.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A sick friend should treat getting better as a <kanji form="大">big</kanji> <kanji form="事">matter</kanji>, barbed to them so they cannot set it down. Telling them so is how you say <vocabulary form="お大事に">take care (get well)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A request for good favor: yoroshiku.
items.meaning_mnemonic: On the two-person boat the deal is simple: <reading>you row, she cooks</reading>. You shake on it and say <reading>よろしく</reading>, asking her to <vocabulary form="よろしく">please treat me well</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Offering something politely: douzo.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You hold the lift doors and wave the next person in, telling them to <reading>do so</reading> before you. You say <reading>どうぞ</reading>, which is <vocabulary form="どうぞ">please (go ahead)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 構（かま）＋いません.
items.mnemonic_text: Not minding it at all: kamaimasen.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Whatever option you pick, this person's <kanji form="構">stance</kanji> does not shift even slightly. A body that stays relaxed no matter what you choose is telling you <vocabulary form="構いません">it doesn't matter</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A stonemason shrugs at a crooked brick and says <reading>come, I'm a mason</reading>. That flat <reading>かまいません</reading> is him telling you <vocabulary form="構いません">it doesn't matter</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（だい）＋丈（じょう）＋夫（ぶ）＋です, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Reassuring that all is well: daijoubu desu.
items.furigana: 大[だい]丈[じょう]夫[ぶ]です
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="大">big</kanji> man built to full <kanji form="丈">measure</kanji> is a <kanji form="夫">man</kanji> nothing knocks over. Point at that sturdy figure and you are saying <vocabulary form="大丈夫です">it's fine / no problem</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 早（さっ）＋速（そく）＋ですが, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A polite way to start business: sassoku desu ga.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The sun is barely <kanji form="早">early</kanji>-morning high and you are already moving <kanji form="速">quick</kanji> on the job. Starting with no small talk like that is <vocabulary form="早速ですが">getting right to it</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Mixed — お ＋ 気（き）on'yomi ＋ に ＋ 召（め）kun'yomi ＋ す.
items.mnemonic_text: Something entering their favored spirit: oki ni mesu.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A fine object <kanji form="召">calls</kanji> out to a person's <kanji form="気">spirit</kanji> and lifts it like steam off a mown field. Something that can do that has managed <vocabulary form="お気に召す">to be pleasing (honorific)</vocabulary>.
items.description: Honorific, and used only about what pleases someone you are raising up, such as a guest, customer, or superior. Never use it for your own likes.

items.word_type: な adjective, adverb, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: A fair amount indeed: kanari.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The pet shop <reading>canary</reading> is louder than a normal bird by a wide margin. Naming that wide margin above ordinary is <reading>かなり</reading>, meaning <vocabulary form="かなり">quite / considerably</vocabulary>.
items.description: Usually an adverb placed right before an adjective, close to fairly or pretty in English. It can also act as a na-adjective before a noun, but that use is much rarer.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 十（じゅう）＋分（ぶん）＋な, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The na-form of juubun: sufficiently enough.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Cut something into <kanji form="十">ten</kanji> <kanji form="分">part</kanji>s and hand someone all ten. Getting the whole set with none missing is what <vocabulary form="十分な">sufficient (attributive)</vocabulary> describes.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 普（ふ）＋通（つう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Widely (普) common (通): normal.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A thing so <kanji form="普">universal</kanji> that it can <kanji form="通">pass through</kanji> any town and nobody looks up is simply <vocabulary form="普通">normal / usual</vocabulary>. As a な adjective it takes な before the noun it describes.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 一（いっ）＋般（ぱん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 一 いち → いっ. Handakuon: 般 はん → ぱん.
items.mnemonic_text: One (一) shared category (般): general.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When <kanji form="一">one</kanji> single rule is broad enough to <kanji form="般">carry</kanji> every person under it, that rule is <vocabulary form="一般">general / common</vocabulary>.

items.word_type: な adjective, adverb, noun, の adjective
items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 特（とく）＋別（べつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Specially (特) separated (別): special.
items.meaning_mnemonic: One cow, held <kanji form="別">separate</kanji> from the market herd for the temple alone, is <kanji form="特">special</kanji>. That set-apart quality is what <vocabulary form="特別">special</vocabulary> means, and as a な adjective the word takes な before its noun.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 重（じゅう）＋要（よう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Heavy (重) and essential (要): important.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Pile a thousand rice sacks onto something you already <kanji form="要">need</kanji>, and the <kanji form="重">heavy</kanji> load makes it impossible to set aside. A need that weighs that much is <vocabulary form="重要">important</vocabulary>, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 大（たい）＋切（せつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Big (大) and cutting (切) close: precious.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture one sharp stroke about to <kanji form="切">cut</kanji> away a <kanji form="大">big</kanji> piece of your life. What you would throw yourself in front of to save is <vocabulary form="大切">important / precious</vocabulary>, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 可（か）＋能（のう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Permissible (可) ability (能): possible.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set an <kanji form="可">approval</kanji> stamp beside the <kanji form="能">ability</kanji> to do the job, and the thing can be done. That is <vocabulary form="可能">possible</vocabulary>, and as a な adjective it takes な before its noun.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋可（か）＋能（のう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Not (不) possible (可能): impossible.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Erase the <kanji form="能">ability</kanji> to do it, erase the fact that it <kanji form="可">can</kanji> be done, then stamp a <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> across what is left, and the thing is flatly <vocabulary form="不可能">impossible</vocabulary>. As a な adjective, it wants な before any noun it describes.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 迷（めい）＋惑（わく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Lost (迷) and confused (惑): a nuisance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone leads you <kanji form="迷">astray</kanji>, then leaves you standing there in <kanji form="惑">perplexity</kanji>, and being dropped in that state by another person is what makes them <vocabulary form="迷惑">annoying / a bother</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な comes before the noun.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 幸（こう）＋福（ふく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Good fortune (幸) and blessing (福): happiness.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Set the homegrown <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> of a stalk in your own soil next to an outright <kanji form="福">blessing</kanji> dropped in your lap, and stacked together they are <vocabulary form="幸福">formal happiness</vocabulary>. This is a な adjective, so な goes in front of the noun it describes.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 幸（しあわ）＋せ.
items.mnemonic_text: A blessed state of being: shiawase.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk you raised yourself, coming up green through your own patch of earth, is the small sure <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> of being <vocabulary form="幸せ">happy / fortunate</vocabulary>. It works as a な adjective, so な sits before the noun.
items.reading_mnemonic: The woman on the bench gives a small wave at nothing whenever her luck turns. That reflex, <reading>she waves</reading>, is <reading>しあわせ</reading>, the tell of someone <vocabulary form="幸せ">happy / fortunate</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 不（ふ）＋幸（こう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Not (不) fortunate (幸): unfortunate.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Draw one hard <kanji form="不">negative</kanji> stroke through that stalk of <kanji form="幸">happiness</kanji> standing in your own soil, and what is left is <vocabulary form="不幸">unfortunate / misfortune</vocabulary>. It is a な adjective, so な comes before the noun it describes.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 気（き）＋楽（らく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Easy (楽) energy (気): carefree.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Let your <kanji form="気">spirit</kanji> rise off you light as steam and everything within reach feel like plain <kanji form="楽">ease</kanji>, and that is what being <vocabulary form="気楽">carefree / relaxed</vocabulary> is. As a な adjective, な comes before the noun it modifies.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 関（かん）＋係（けい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A barrier (関) tied (係): a relationship.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Run a cord from one person to another and pull your end of it. Whatever happens to the one is felt straight down the line by the other, and that living line between them is a <vocabulary form="関係">relationship / connection</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 興（きょう）＋味（み）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Rising (興) flavor (味): interest.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A subject that keeps <kanji form="興">entertaining</kanji> you and leaves a <kanji form="味">taste</kanji> you go back for again has a hold on you. That hold is your <vocabulary form="興味">interest</vocabulary> in it.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 希（き）＋望（ぼう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A rare (希) view ahead (望): hope.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Fix your mind on the thing you want and hold the picture of it bright even while it is still far off. Refusing to let that picture go dim is <vocabulary form="希望">hope / wish</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 目（もく）＋的（てき）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: An eye's (目) target (的): a purpose.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Fix your <kanji form="目">eye</kanji> on the <kanji form="的">target</kanji> at the far end of the range and let everything else blur. That one held point is your <vocabulary form="目的">purpose / goal</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 方（ほう）＋法（ほう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A direction's (方) rule (法): a method.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Which <kanji form="方">direction</kanji> you choose to come at a task from is your <vocabulary form="方法">method</vocabulary> for getting it done. Pick a different way in and you have a different method.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 条（じょう）＋件（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: An article's (条) piece (件): a condition.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Each <kanji form="条">clause</kanji> written into the agreement names one <kanji form="件">matter</kanji> that has to be settled before anything moves ahead. Every one of those clauses is a <vocabulary form="条件">condition</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 提（てい）＋案（あん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Presenting (提) a plan (案): a proposal.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="提">carry</kanji> a worked-out <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> in your hands to the meeting and lay it flat on the table for the room. Set out to be judged like that, it is a <vocabulary form="提案">proposal</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 機（き）＋械（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mechanism's (機) frame (械): a machine.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A cabinet packed with gears and levers that turns one small push at the handle into the same heavy job done over and over is a <vocabulary form="機械">machine</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 機（き）＋会（かい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mechanism's (機) meeting (会): a chance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="機">mechanism</kanji> of events turns, and for one moment a gap in it lines up with you. Step through and <kanji form="会">meet</kanji> it and you have taken an <vocabulary form="機会">opportunity</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 場（ば）＋合（あい）.
items.mnemonic_text: A place's (場) fit (合): a case.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Take one <kanji form="場">place</kanji> and one particular way the details inside it <kanji form="合">fit</kanji> together. That exact arrangement is the <vocabulary form="場合">case / situation</vocabulary> you are talking about.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 事（じ）＋情（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A matter's (事) feeling (情): circumstances.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A single <kanji form="事">matter</kanji> sitting at the centre of an event drags a whole knot of <kanji form="情">feelings</kanji> in behind it. That full tangle around it is the <vocabulary form="事情">circumstances</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 感（かん）＋情（じょう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A feeling's (感) sentiment (情): emotion.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The whole <kanji form="感">feeling</kanji> hitting you at once, with the head left out of it entirely, settles into one named <vocabulary form="感情">emotion</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 性（せい）＋格（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One's nature's (性) frame (格): personality.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your inborn <kanji form="性">nature</kanji> gets worn over years into a fixed <kanji form="格">rank</kanji> of habits and set reactions. That settled shape is what others call your <vocabulary form="性格">personality</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 態（たい）＋度（ど）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A shaped (態) measure (度): attitude.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Measure how many <kanji form="度">degrees</kanji> a person leans toward or away from what is put in front of them. That tilt, read off face and posture, is their <vocabulary form="態度">attitude</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 技（ぎ）＋術（じゅつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A skill's (技) craft (術): technology.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Years of drills turn shaky hands into hands that can build or fix almost anything. That hard-won ability is your <vocabulary form="技術">technology / skill</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 科（か）＋学（がく）＋者（しゃ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A science's (科学) person (者): a scientist.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="者">person</kanji> who spends every day turning pages in one narrow <kanji form="科">department</kanji> of <kanji form="学">study</kanji> is a <vocabulary form="科学者">scientist</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 発（はつ）＋明（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Emitting (発) a bright (明) idea: invention.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="明">bright</kanji> idea that <kanji form="発">departs</kanji> your head and turns into a working thing on the bench is an <vocabulary form="発明">invention</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 研（けん）＋究（きゅう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Grinding (研) to investigate (究): research.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="研">polish</kanji> one question for years and dig in a cave for its bottom. That patient <kanji form="究">study</kanji> of a thing down to its base is <vocabulary form="研究">research</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 実（じっ）＋験（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 実 じつ → じっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A real (実) examination (験): an experiment.
items.meaning_mnemonic: To run an <vocabulary form="実験">experiment</vocabulary> is to <kanji form="験">examine</kanji>, under controlled conditions, whether an idea holds up against <kanji form="実">reality</kanji>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 調（ちょう）＋査（さ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Checking (調) to examine (査): a survey.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="調">investigate</kanji> once by putting the question to every face in the crowd, then <kanji form="査">investigate</kanji> again to be sure. Two passes over the same ground make an <vocabulary form="調査">investigation / survey</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 報（ほう）＋告（こく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Repaying (報) an announcement (告): a report.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you stand up and formally <kanji form="告">tell</kanji> the room exactly what happened, start to finish, what you have given is a <vocabulary form="報告">report</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 会（かい）＋議（ぎ）＋室（しつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A meeting's (会議) room (室): a meeting room.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Every hallway in the building ends at one <kanji form="室">room</kanji> kept for people to <kanji form="会">meet</kanji> and <kanji form="議">debate</kanji> in. That is the <vocabulary form="会議室">meeting room</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Irregular — うけつけ cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 受付.
items.mnemonic_text: Receiving (受) and attaching (付): the front desk.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The first desk inside the door <kanji form="受">accepts</kanji> your name and <kanji form="付">attaches</kanji> you to the person you came to see. That desk is the <vocabulary form="受付">reception (desk)</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A bowing front-desk clerk greets every visitor with the same line: 「OK, <reading>take a key</reading>.」 Blur those words together and you hear <reading>うけつけ</reading>, the <vocabulary form="受付">reception (desk)</vocabulary> where everyone checks in.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 案（あん）＋内（ない）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A plan (案) leading inside (内): guidance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Someone who holds the whole <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> of a place in their head can lead you <kanji form="内">inside</kanji> it without a wrong turn, and that service is <vocabulary form="案内">guidance / information</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 案（あん）＋内（ない）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: To lead someone with a plan: annai suru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You walk ahead of the visitor with the floor <kanji form="案">plan</kanji> clear in your mind and name each room <kanji form="内">inside</kanji> as you open its door. Doing that for someone is <vocabulary form="案内する">to guide / show around</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 注（ちゅう）＋意（い）＋する, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Pouring (注) meaning (意): to be careful.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji form="注">Pour</kanji> your whole <kanji form="意">mind</kanji> onto one spot and hold it there. That single act is what it means <vocabulary form="注意する">to pay attention / warn</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 記（き）＋録（ろく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Recording (記) and noting (録): a record.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="記">scribe</kanji> writes down exactly what happened and keeps himself out of every line. That filed account, kept for checking years later, is a <vocabulary form="記録">record</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 放（ほう）＋送（そう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Releasing (放) and sending (送): a broadcast.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="放">set free</kanji> a voice into the air and <kanji form="送">send</kanji> it out to every radio in the country at once. That single push to everyone is a <vocabulary form="放送">broadcast</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 口（こう）＋座（ざ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A mouth's (口) seat (座): an account.
items.meaning_mnemonic: At the bank your money gets a reserved place to <kanji form="座">sit</kanji>, and a slot shaped like a <kanji form="口">mouth</kanji> in the counter is where you feed it in. That spot where your money sits is your <vocabulary form="口座">bank account</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 預（よ）＋金（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Entrusted (預) money (金): a deposit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Hand your gold coins across the bank counter for safe keeping instead of spending them, and the <kanji form="金">money</kanji> the bank now holds for you is your <vocabulary form="預金">savings / deposit</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 借（しゃっ）＋金（きん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 借 しゃく → しゃっ.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed (借) money (金): a debt.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="金">money</kanji> you <kanji form="借">borrow</kanji> today and keep putting off paying back, month after month, is your <vocabulary form="借金">debt</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 保（ほ）＋険（けん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Protection (保) danger (険): insurance.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You pay a little now to <kanji form="保">keep a guarantee</kanji> that pays out later, when the road turns <kanji form="険">steep and dangerous</kanji>. That standing promise is <vocabulary form="保険">insurance</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 契（けい）＋約（やく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A pledged (契) promise (約): a contract.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Two people each make a <kanji form="契">pledge</kanji>, write the matching <kanji form="約">promise</kanji> down, and sign it. That signed pair of promises is a <vocabulary form="契約">contract</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 署（しょ）＋名（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A signed office's (署) name (名): a signature.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A page cannot see your face, so you prove it is you by writing your <kanji form="名">name</kanji> across the bottom in your own hand. That mark is your <vocabulary form="署名">signature</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: The name stamp used instead of a signature: hanko.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture your family name carved into a small red-inked <reading>hunk o'</reading> boxwood that you press onto every official form. That carved 「<reading>はんこ</reading>」 is your <vocabulary form="はんこ">personal seal (stamp)</vocabulary>, and it signs for you all over Japan.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 弁（べん）＋護（ご）＋士（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One who speaks (弁) in protection (護): a lawyer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="士">scholar</kanji> you hire to <kanji form="護">protect</kanji> you works the case like a <kanji form="弁">valve</kanji>, opening and shutting what the court is allowed to hear. Someone who guards you by controlling that flow is a <vocabulary form="弁護士">lawyer</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 警（けい）＋察（さつ）＋官（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A police (警察) official (官): an officer.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="官">bureaucrat</kanji> paid to <kanji form="警">admonish</kanji> lawbreakers and <kanji form="察">surmise</kanji> which of them did it is a <vocabulary form="警察官">police officer</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 消（しょう）＋防（ぼう）＋士（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: One who extinguishes (消) defense (防): a firefighter.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A trained <kanji form="士">samurai</kanji> of the fire station, sent in to <kanji form="消">extinguish</kanji> a blaze and <kanji form="防">defend</kanji> the next street from it, is a <vocabulary form="消防士">firefighter</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 海（かい）＋岸（がん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The sea's (海) bank (岸): a coast.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Where the <kanji form="海">sea</kanji> that every river drains into finally meets the <kanji form="岸">beach</kanji>, you are standing on the <vocabulary form="海岸">coast / seashore</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 島（しま）.
items.mnemonic_text: A bird (鳥) resting on a mountain (山): an island.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A scrap of land with open sea on every side of it, no bridge and no road off, is an <vocabulary form="島">island</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Shig the shipwrecked sailor rows for days toward a green <reading>shimmer</reading> on the horizon. When he drags his boat ashore he names the place 「<reading>しま</reading>」, his own <vocabulary form="島">island</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 野（の）＋山（やま）.
items.mnemonic_text: Wide fields (野) and mountains (山): the countryside.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The open <kanji form="野">plains</kanji> the village never fenced, set against the <kanji form="山">mountain</kanji> at their back, are together the <vocabulary form="野山">fields and mountains</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Irregular — いなか cannot be assembled from the dictionary readings of 田舎.
items.mnemonic_text: Rice fields (田) beside a hut (舎): the countryside.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A view that is nothing but flooded <kanji form="田">rice paddy</kanji> and one lonely <kanji form="舎">hut</kanji> at its edge is the <vocabulary form="田舎">countryside</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Nao the delivery gecko groans that every run out here means three hours <reading>in a car</reading>. That long haul to 「<reading>いなか</reading>」 is just what visiting the <vocabulary form="田舎">countryside</vocabulary> costs.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 都（と）＋市（し）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The capital's (都) market (市): a city.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji form="都">metropolis</kanji> built up by constant new arrivals, with a <kanji form="市">market</kanji> square beating at its center, is a <vocabulary form="都市">city (urban)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 首（しゅ）＋都（と）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The head (首) city (都): a capital.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The single <kanji form="首">neck</kanji> that the whole <kanji form="都">metropolis</kanji> turns its head on, the city every decision has to pass through, is the <vocabulary form="首都">capital (city)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 地（ち）＋方（ほう）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: The ground's (地) direction (方): a region.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A stretch of <kanji form="地">ground</kanji> marked off by which <kanji form="方">direction</kanji> it lies from the capital is a <vocabulary form="地方">region / countryside</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 国（こっ）＋家（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 国 こく → こっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A country's (国) household (家): a nation.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Treat the whole <kanji form="国">country</kanji>, walls and shared jewel and all, as one <kanji form="家">house</kanji> that everyone inside it belongs to, and you have a <vocabulary form="国家">nation / state</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 文（ぶん）＋明（めい）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Writing's (文) brightness (明): civilization.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When a people's <kanji form="文">literature</kanji> grows <kanji form="明">bright</kanji> enough to light the road for everyone who comes after, that shared glow is a <vocabulary form="文明">civilization</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 生（せい）＋活（かつ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Life (生) in motion (活): daily living.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Your <kanji form="生">life</kanji> seen as the <kanji form="活">lively</kanji>, day-to-day business of eating, washing and getting by is your <vocabulary form="生活">life / living</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 習（しゅう）＋慣（かん）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Learning (習) that becomes routine (慣): a habit.
items.meaning_mnemonic: Something you once had to <kanji form="習">practice</kanji> on purpose and are now so <kanji form="慣">accustomed</kanji> to that you do it without thinking has turned into a <vocabulary form="習慣">custom / habit</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 日（にっ）＋記（き）, each kanji read with its on'yomi. Gemination: 日 にち → にっ.
items.mnemonic_text: A day's (日) record (記): a diary.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A written <kanji form="記">account</kanji> that breaks the usual rule and is only ever about your own <kanji form="日">day</kanji> is a <vocabulary form="日記">diary</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 行（おこな）＋う.
items.mnemonic_text: Carrying an action all the way through: okonau.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You <kanji form="行">go</kanji> from talking about a plan to running it for real. Taking a ceremony or a survey and actually staging it is what it means to <vocabulary form="行う">carry out / conduct</vocabulary> it.
items.reading_mnemonic: Koichi opens every konbini restock drill by clapping once and calling 「<reading>OK, now</reading>」. That is his cue to 「<reading>おこなう</reading>」 the plan, to <vocabulary form="行う">carry out / conduct</vocabulary> it exactly as written.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 参（さん）＋加（か）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Joining (参) and adding (加): participation.
items.meaning_mnemonic: You stop watching from the side and start <kanji form="参">going</kanji> along with the group. Once you <kanji form="加">add</kanji> yourself to the people actually doing the thing, that is <vocabulary form="参加">participation (noun)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 行（ぎょう）＋事（じ）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: A carried-out (行) matter (事): an event.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="事">matter</kanji> that the whole calendar has to <kanji form="行">go</kanji> ahead with on one fixed date is an <vocabulary form="行事">event / function</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 祭（まつ）＋り.
items.mnemonic_text: An altar (示) celebrated openly: a festival.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A village <kanji form="祭">ritual</kanji> for the local gods, once the whole street piles on food stalls, drums and lanterns, has grown into a <vocabulary form="祭り">festival</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Tomo the tanuki knows the shrine <reading>mats really</reading> fill up fast once the drums start. He stakes out his spot for the 「<reading>まつり</reading>」 hours before the <vocabulary form="祭り">festival</vocabulary> begins.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 花（はな）＋火（び）.
items.mnemonic_text: Flower (花) fire (火): fireworks.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="火">fire</kanji> that bursts open in the sky as a huge <kanji form="花">flower</kanji> of coloured sparks is what <vocabulary form="花火">fireworks</vocabulary> are.

items.reading_composition: Jukugo — 将（しょう）＋来（らい）＋計（けい）＋画（かく）, each kanji read with its on'yomi.
items.mnemonic_text: Plans (計画) for the future (将来).
items.furigana: 将[しょう]来[らい]計[けい]画[かく]
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="将">general</kanji> decides which battles are still to <kanji form="来">come</kanji>, counts them out as a quiet <kanji form="計">plot</kanji>, and draws the whole campaign in a single <kanji form="画">brush-stroke</kanji>. That stroke showing what lies ahead is a <vocabulary form="将来計画">future plan</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — 引（ひ）＋っ＋越（こ）＋し.
items.mnemonic_text: Pulling (引っ) your life over (越し): a move.
items.meaning_mnemonic: When you <kanji form="引">pull</kanji> the last box off the old floor and <kanji form="越">cross over</kanji> into an empty new flat, that whole change of address is <vocabulary form="引っ越し">moving (residence, noun)</vocabulary>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: What you throw away: gomi.
items.meaning_mnemonic: The raccoon works the alley bins like a <reading>gourmet</reading> picking a buffet, but every fish skeleton, mouldy rice ball, and coffee filter it drags out is just <vocabulary form="ごみ">trash / garbage</vocabulary>. The raccoon's five-star spread is <reading>ごみ</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kun'yomi — ごみ＋箱（ばこ）. Rendaku: 箱 はこ → ばこ.
items.mnemonic_text: A box (箱) for trash (ごみ): a trash can.
items.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji form="箱">box</kanji> whose only job is to hold the trash you throw out all day is a <vocabulary form="ごみ箱">trash can</vocabulary>.
items.reading_mnemonic: A <reading>gummy bucket</reading> by the school gate, its rim sticky with old soda, swallows every wrapper and juice box the kids drop until it is the field's one huge <vocabulary form="ごみ箱">trash can</vocabulary>. That sticky bucket is a <reading>ごみばこ</reading>.

items.reading_composition: Kana only — the word is written exactly as it is read.
items.mnemonic_text: Borrowed word: risaikuru.
items.meaning_mnemonic: <reading>Lisa cycles</reading> one loop over and over: bottle bank, crusher, shop, back to the bottle bank. Running that same can around the circle until it becomes a brand-new can is <vocabulary form="リサイクル">recycling</vocabulary>, the loop you hear in <reading>リサイクル</reading>.
